nodes.name: Lemma B.2
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a causal DAG $\mathcal{G}$. Let $A \notin \mathbf{Y}$ be a node and consider a path $p$ from $A$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ in $\mathcal{G}$. If  $p$ is blocked by $\mathbf{Z}$ and open given $\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Z}$, then there exists a proper non-causal path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ that is open given $\mathbf{Z}$.
nodes.section: Figure 11: Proof structure of Proposition 3.1.

nodes.name: Lemma B.5
nodes.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be nodes in a causal DAG $\mathcal{G}$. Let $\mathbf{Z}$ be a node set in $\mathcal{G}$, such that $Y \notin \mathbf{Z}, \mathrm{pa}(X,\mathcal{G}) \subseteq \mathbf{Z}$ and $\mathrm{de}(X,\mathcal{G}) \cap \mathbf{Z} = \emptyset$. Then $\mathbf{Z}$ is a valid adjustment set relative to $(X,Y)$.

nodes.name: Lemma B.4
nodes.statement:
Consider a causal DAG $\mathcal{G}=(\mathbf{V},\mathbf{E})$, let $\mathbf{V}$ follow a causal linear model compatible with $\mathcal{G}$ and let $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}= \{\epsilon_{v_1},\dots, \epsilon_{v_p}\}$ be the set of errors from the underlying causal linear model. Given a node $A$ and a node set $\mathbf{W}=\{W_1,\dots,W_k\}$, such that $A \notin \mathbf{W}$, the residual $\delta_{a\mathbf{w}}$ is a function of some minimally sized subset $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{a\mathbf{w}}$ of $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}$. 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Let $M \in \mathbf{W}$. If $\epsilon_m \in \boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{a\mathbf{w}}$, then there exists a path of the form 
		$
		A \dots \rightarrow M,
		$
		that is open given $\mathbf{W}$.  
		\item Let $M \notin \mathbf{W}$. If $\epsilon_m \in \boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{a\mathbf{w}}$, then there exists  a directed path from $M$ to some node $M' \in (\{A\} \cup \mathbf{W})$ that is open given $\{A\} \cup \mathbf{W}$ and $\epsilon_{m'} \in \epsilon^{a\mathbf{w}}$. Consequentially, there exists a path from $A$ to $M$ that is open given $\mathbf{W}$.
		 		






	\end{enumerate}
nodes.section: Figure 11: Proof structure of Proposition 3.1.

nodes.name: Lemma B.6
nodes.statement: Let $A$ and $M$ be two nodes and $\mathbf{W}$ a node set in a DAG $\mathcal{G}$, such that $A \notin \mathbf{W}$ and $M \in \mathbf{W}$. Let $\mathbf{P} = \mathrm{pa}(M,\mathcal{G}) \setminus \mathbf{W}$. If no path from $A$ to $M$, ending with an edge into $M$ that is open given $\mathbf{W}$ exists, then $\mathbf{P} \perp_{\mathcal{G}} A | \mathbf{W}$.

nodes.name: Lemma C.2
nodes.statement:
Let $(\mathbf{X}^T,\mathbf{Y}^T,\mathbf{T}^T,\mathbf{S}^T, \mathbf{W}^T)^T$, with $\mathbf{T}, \mathbf{S}$ and $\mathbf{W}$ possibly of length zero, be
	 a mean $\mathbf{0}$ random vector with finite variance, such that $\mathbf{X}=(X_1,\dots,X_{k_x})^T$ and $\mathbf{Y} = (Y_1,\dots,Y_{k_y})^T$. If $\mathbf{T} \protect\mathpalette{\protect\mathrel{\rlap{$}\perp$}\mkern2mu{}\perp}} \mathbf{Y} | \mathbf{W},\mathbf{S},\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{S} \protect\mathpalette{\protect\mathrel{\rlap{$}\perp$}\mkern2mu{}\perp}} \mathbf{X} | \mathbf{W},\mathbf{T}$, 
	then
	\begin{enumerate}[ label = (\alph*)]
		\item $\sigma_{x_ix_i.\mathbf{x_{-i}wt}} \leq \sigma_{x_ix_i.\mathbf{x_{-i}ws}} \ \textrm{and}$
		
		\item $\sigma_{y_jy_j.\mathbf{xws}} \leq \sigma_{y_jy_j.\mathbf{xwt}},$
		
	\end{enumerate}
for all $i \in \{1,\dots,k_x\}$ and $j \in \{1,\dots, k_y\}$.

nodes.name: Lemma C.5
nodes.statement:
Let $(\mathbf{X}^T,\mathbf{Y}^T,\mathbf{S}^T,\mathbf{T}^T)^T$, with $\mathbf{S}$ possibly of length zero, be a mean $\mathbf{0}$ random vector with finite variance. If $\mathbf{T} \protect\mathpalette{\protect\mathrel{\rlap{$}\perp$}\mkern2mu{}\perp}} \mathbf{X} | \mathbf{S}$ or $\mathbf{T} \protect\mathpalette{\protect\mathrel{\rlap{$}\perp$}\mkern2mu{}\perp}} \mathbf{Y} | \mathbf{X}, \mathbf{S}$, then
$
\boldsymbol{\beta}_{\mathbf{yx}.\mathbf{s}} = \boldsymbol{\beta}_{\mathbf{yx}.\mathbf{st}}.
$
Furthermore, if $\mathbf{T} \protect\mathpalette{\protect\mathrel{\rlap{$}\perp$}\mkern2mu{}\perp}} \mathbf{Y}| \mathbf{X} , \mathbf{S}$, then
$
\Sigma_{\mathbf{yy}.\mathbf{xst}} = \Sigma_{\mathbf{yy}.\mathbf{xs}}.$

nodes.name: Lemma E.4
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a causal DAG $\mathcal{G}$, such that $\mathbf{Y} \subseteq \mathrm{de}(\mathbf{X},\mathcal{G})$ and let $\mathbf{O}=\mathbf{O}(\mathbf{X,Y},\mathcal{G})$. Let $\mathbf{T}$ be a set such that 
	$\mathbf{T} \cap (\mathrm{forb}(\mathbf{X,Y},\mathcal{G}) \cup \mathbf{O}) = \emptyset$. If there exists a valid adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in $\mathcal{G}$, then $\mathbf{Y} \perp_{\mathcal{G}}\mathbf{T}|\mathbf{O} \cup \mathbf{X}$.
nodes.section: Figure 13: Proof structure of Proposition E.1.

nodes.name: Lemma E.3
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a causal DAG $\mathcal{G}$, such that $\mathbf{Y} \subseteq \mathrm{de}(\mathbf{X},\mathcal{G})$ and let $\mathbf{O}=\mathbf{O}(\mathbf{X,Y},\mathcal{G})$. Let $\mathbf{T}$ be a node set such that $\mathbf{T} \cap \mathrm{de}(\mathrm{cn}(\mathbf{X,Y},\mathcal{G}),\mathcal{G}) = \emptyset$ and $\mathbf{T} \cap \mathbf{O} = \emptyset$. If an adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\mathcal{G}$ exists, then all proper non-causal paths from $\mathbf{T}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ in $\mathcal{G}$ that contain no nodes from $\mathbf{X} \setminus \mathbf{T}$ are blocked by $\mathbf{O} \cup (\mathbf{X} \setminus \mathbf{T})$.
nodes.section: Figure 13: Proof structure of Proposition E.1.

nodes.name: Lemma E.5
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y},\mathbf{S}$ and $\mathbf{W}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a causal DAG $\mathcal{G}$, such that $\mathbf{Y} \subseteq \mathrm{de}(\mathbf{X},\mathcal{G})$, let $\mathbf{O}=\mathbf{O}(\mathbf{X,Y},\mathcal{G})$ and assume that $\mathbf{S}  \subseteq \mathbf{O}$. If $\mathbf{W}$ is a valid adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in $\mathcal{G}$, then $\mathbf{X} \perp_{\mathcal{G}} \mathbf{S}| \mathbf{W}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.4
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a maximal PDAG{} $\mathcal{G} = (\mathbf{V},\mathbf{E})$, such that $\mathbf{V}$ follows a causal linear model that is compatible with $\mathcal{G}$. Let $\mathbf{Z_1}$ and $\mathbf{Z_2}$ be two valid adjustment sets relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\mathcal{G}$ and let $\mathbf{T}=\mathbf{Z_1} \setminus \mathbf{Z_2}$ and $\mathbf{S}=\mathbf{Z_2} \setminus \mathbf{Z_1}$. 
	If $\mathbf{Y} \perp_{\mathcal{G}} \mathbf{T} | \mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Z_2} $ and $\mathbf{X} \perp_{\mathcal{G}} \mathbf{S} | \mathbf{Z_1}$,
	then 
	\[
	a.var(\hat{\tau}_{\mathbf{yx}}^{\mathbf{z_2}}) \leq 
	a.var(\hat{\tau}_{\mathbf{yx}}^{\mathbf{z_1}}),
	\]
	
	with the matrix inequality denoting entry wise inequality.
nodes.section: Figure 13: Proof structure of Proposition E.1.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.13
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a causal maximal PDAG{} $\mathcal{G} = (\mathbf{V},\mathbf{E})$, such that $\mathbf{Y} \subseteq \mathrm{possde}(\mathbf{X},\mathcal{G})$. Let the density $f$ of $\mathbf{V}$ be compatible with $\mathcal{G}$ and let $\mathbf{O}=\mathbf{O}(\mathbf{X,Y},\mathcal{G})$. Then the following three statements hold:
	\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
		\item The set $\mathbf{O}$ is a valid adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\mathcal{G}$ if and only if there exists a valid adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\mathcal{G}$. 
		\item Let $\mathbf{Z}$ be a valid adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in $\mathcal{G}$. If $\mathbf{V}$ follows a causal linear model compatible with $\mathcal{G}$ then
		\[
		a.var(\hat{\tau}^{\mathbf{o}}_{\mathbf{yx}}) \leq a.var(\hat{\tau}^{\mathbf{z}}_{\mathbf{yx}}).
		\]
		\item Let $\mathbf{Z}$ be a valid adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in $\mathcal{G}$, such that 
		\[
		a.var(\hat{\tau}^{\mathbf{o}}_{\mathbf{yx}}) = a.var(\hat{\tau}^{\mathbf{z}}_{\mathbf{yx}}).
		\]
		If $\mathbf{V}$ follows a causal linear model compatible with $\mathcal{G}$ and $f$ is faithful to $\mathcal{G}$ then $\mathbf{O}\subseteq \mathbf{Z}$. 
	\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Lemma E.7
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a maximal PDAG{} $\mathcal{G}$, such that $\mathcal{G}$ is amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$, $\mathbf{Y} \subseteq \mathrm{possde}(\mathbf{X},\mathcal{G})$ and let $\mathcal{D}$ be a DAG in $[\mathcal{G}]$.
	Then  
	$\mathbf{O}(\mathbf{X,Y},\mathcal{D}) = \mathbf{O}(\mathbf{X,Y},\mathcal{G})$.
nodes.section: Figure 14: Proof structure of Theorem 3.13 for CPDAGs and maximal PDAGs.

nodes.name: Lemma E.6
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a maximal PDAG{} $\mathcal{G}$, such that $\mathcal{G}$ is amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$. Then for every node $W \in \mathrm{possde}(\mathrm{posscn}(\mathbf{X,Y},\mathcal{G}),\mathcal{G})$

	there is a path $p_W = ( X = V_1, V_2, \dots ,V_k=W ), k > 1$ from $\mathbf{X}$ to $W$, such that 
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
		
		\item $p_W$ is proper, and 
		\item $p_W = X \rightarrow V_1 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow W$. 
	\end{enumerate}
	Note that if $\mathbf{Y} \subseteq \mathrm{possde}(\mathbf{X},\mathcal{G})$, this implies that $\mathbf{Y} \subseteq \mathrm{de}(\mathbf{X},\mathcal{G})$ and $\mathbf{Y} \subseteq \mathrm{cn}(\mathbf{X,Y},\mathcal{G})$.
nodes.section: Figure 14: Proof structure of Theorem 3.13 for CPDAGs and maximal PDAGs.

nodes.name: Lemma E.8
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a maximal PDAG{} $\mathcal{G}$, such that $\mathcal{G}$ is amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ and let $\mathcal{D}$ be a DAG in $[\mathcal{G}]$. Then
	$\mathrm{forb}(\mathbf{X,Y},\mathcal{G}) = \mathrm{forb}(\mathbf{X,Y},\mathcal{D})$.
